newsitem.title: USA: IBM files $3 bln shelf for debt, stocks.
newsitem.headline: IBM files $3 bln shelf for debt, stocks.

text.p: International Business Machines said Tuesday it filed a shelf registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission to sell up $3 billion in debt securities, capital and preferred stock.
When combined with a previous registration, IBM will have a total offering of $3,230,000,000 in securities available for sale, the filing said.
The offering also includes depositary shares and warrants to purchase the debt securities and preferred and capital stock.

Net proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, IBM said in the filing. The company said that it expects that it will, on a recurring basis, engage in additional financing in character and amount to be determined when the need arises.

IBM, based in Armonk, New York, develops, manufactures and sells advanced information processing products, including computers and microelectronic technology, software, networking systems and information technology-related services.
